title: Dedicated pools: add regional defaults + guardrails for networking/IAM inputs
author: Keiko Yamamoto
description: Context: As part of the provision-to-ready automation work, we want pool creation/expansion to be repeatable across regions with fewer “human memory” dependencies and fewer late failures during bootstrap/validation. Today, module consumers must supply a large set of region-specific networking and IAM inputs, and mis-wiring (wrong subnet types, wrong role/policy, missing VPC endpoints) tends to fail late (kube bootstrap, image pulls, control-plane registration). Changes: (1) Add opinionated regional defaults for Dedicated pool creation (AWS) keyed by region (e.g., us-east-1/us-west-2/eu-west-1) including VPC/subnet selection strategy, default security group rules, and required VPC endpoints for private clusters; (2) Add guardrails via variable validation + terraform preconditions to fail fast on known bad configs: disallow public subnets for worker nodes, require >=2 subnets across >=2 AZs, enforce that node role ARNs match the Dedicated boundary policy prefix, and require explicit opt-in for any “custom IAM role” usage; (3) Document required variables and the “minimal inputs” path (region + pool_id + capacity + sku) in module README, plus a worked example for a brand new pool and a pool expansion; (4) Add standardized outputs (node_role_arn, cluster_subnet_ids, selected_vpc_id) that the orchestrator will consume, aligned with PR #913’s idempotent apply work. Notes: Defaults are designed to be overridable; the intent is to make the common path safe and easy while keeping escape hatches for edge cases. Testing: terraform fmt/validate; plan applied in staging for a new internal pool (no infra changes beyond expected resources); verified precondition failures on misconfigured subnet inputs; verified IAM role validation catches accidentally passing admin roles. Rollout: land behind module minor bump; orchestrator can adopt defaults gradually per region.
commits: modules/dedicated-pool: add subnet/IAM validations and preconditions
docs: update README with required vars + minimal examples
outputs: standardize networking/IAM outputs for orchestration consumption
tests: add basic terratest-style validation harness for input guardrails
changed_areas: modules/dedicated-pool/variables.tf (new validations; deprecations noted in comments)
modules/dedicated-pool/iam.tf (role boundary checks + custom role opt-in)
ci_checks: checkov: pass (1 skipped with justification in code comment: allow egress-all on node SG due to controlled outbound via NAT + egress filtering at VPC firewall layer)
review_conversation: Nina Petrova (review): Can we avoid hardcoding VPC IDs in regional defaults? We’ve had churn when staging/prod differ. Suggest defaulting to tags (env + region + purpose) and allowing explicit override for legacy VPCs.

Keiko Yamamoto (author): Good call. Updated selectors to prefer tagged VPC/subnets (redwood:purpose=dedicated-pool, redwood:env, redwood:region) and only allow explicit IDs via override vars; docs updated with tagging requirements.

Victor Alvarez (review): Subnet guardrail: please ensure we’re checking for private subnets (no map_public_ip_on_launch) but also that route table doesn’t go straight to IGW. Terraform can’t easily introspect route tables here; can we at least require NAT gateway IDs OR explicit allow_public_subnets=true?

Keiko Yamamoto (author): Added explicit allow_public_subnets boolean (default false) + validation error message. We can’t reliably inspect route tables without data sources that add eventual-consistency flakiness; this gives us a safe default and an audited override path.
Miles Thornton (review): Multi-region: do we have defaults for ap-southeast-1 yet? Also, please ensure error messages include the region/pool_id for easier debugging in orchestrator logs.

Keiko Yamamoto (author): Not adding APAC defaults in this PR (kept scope to regions used in the sprint pilot). Added region/pool_id to all precondition messages and surfaced selected values in outputs so logs can print them.

Marcus Lin (review): IAM guardrail looks good; please ensure custom role opt-in is explicit and that we validate the permissions boundary is set. Also, add a note in README about least-privilege and boundary requirement.

Keiko Yamamoto (author): Added precondition: when custom_node_role_arn is set, require custom_role_permissions_boundary_arn and validate it matches our boundary policy prefix; README updated with rationale and expected naming.
Vanessa Ortiz (review): This unblocks orchestration consuming stable outputs. Request: call out required vars vs optional vars clearly in docs; operators keep asking which inputs are mandatory.
Keiko Yamamoto (author): Reworked README “Inputs” section into Required/Optional, added a minimal example block, and added a troubleshooting section mapping common validation failures to fixes.
Miles Thornton (final): Looks good. Please confirm version bump semantics (minor) and that existing callers won’t break.

Keiko Yamamoto (author): Confirmed: no required variable additions; new variables have defaults; validations only tighten behavior when previously-dangerous combinations were used (now fail fast). Version bump to v0.19.0.
Nina Petrova (approve): Approved after tag-based selectors change.
release_notes: Terraform module update: adds region-aware defaults and fail-fast guardrails for Dedicated pool creation (networking + IAM), plus clearer documentation of required variables and standardized outputs for orchestration.
